name: The Karpathy/Lütke origin tweets (June 2025)
publisher: Individual posts on X (Twitter) by Tobi Lütke (CEO, Shopify) and Andrej Karpathy (independent AI researcher, formerly OpenAI/Tesla, founder of Eureka Labs)
date_published: Tobi Lütke, X post, June 19, 2025, ~03:01 UTC (status/1935533422589399127). Andrej Karpathy, X post, June 25, 2025, ~15:54 UTC (status/1937902205765607626), six days later, explicitly endorsing Lütke's term.
claim_value: Lütke (June 19, 2025): "I really like the term 'context engineering' over prompt engineering. It describes the core skill better: the art of providing all the context for the task to be plausibly solvable by the LLM." Karpathy (June 25, 2025): "+1 for 'context engineering' over 'prompt engineering'. People associate prompts with short task descriptions you'd give an LLM in your day-to-day use. When in every industrial-strength LLM app, context engineering is the delicate art and science of filling the context window with just the right information for the next step," going on to list the inputs in play (task descriptions/explanations, few-shot examples, RAG, related multimodal data, tools, state and history, compaction) and warning that too little or the wrong-shaped context leaves the LLM unable to perform well, while too much raises cost and can itself degrade performance.
claim_definition: A historical/coinage fact: this is the specific two-tweet exchange the industry points to as the moment 'context engineering' displaced 'prompt engineering' as the preferred term. Lütke proposed the relabeling first; Karpathy, with a much larger and more technically-credentialed following, publicly seconded it six days later and gave it a fuller technical definition (the context window as the thing being 'filled' with the right information, not just a prompt being written). The exchange itself contains no benchmark or empirical claim, only a definitional/terminological one.
reproducibility: Not applicable: this is a dated public social-media post, not an empirical or benchmark claim. The tweets themselves are independently verifiable by their status URLs and by Twitter/X's snowflake-ID timestamp encoding, which was used here to confirm the exact UTC posting times (June 19, 2025 for Lütke's post; June 25, 2025 for Karpathy's) independent of any secondary source's paraphrase. [uncertain: exact verbatim wording could not be re-fetched directly from x.com in this research pass, since x.com blocked automated fetching; wording below is reconstructed from search-engine snippets that quote the tweets directly, not from a direct screenshot or API read of the live post.]
publisher_sells_relevant_product: No. Shopify (Lütke) sells an e-commerce platform, not a context-engineering, vector-database, or LLM-tooling product; any benefit to Shopify from the term's popularity is indirect (Shopify has shipped AI shopping/agent features, but the tweet itself is not product marketing). Karpathy sells no product related to the term; he was between ventures/at Eureka Labs at the time and has no commercial stake in 'context engineering' as a category.
conflict_notes: Several outlets and summaries (seen in this search pass) describe the origin as 'mid-2025' without dates, or round Lütke's post to 'June 18, 2025' rather than June 19. Snowflake-ID decoding of status 1935533422589399127 places it at 2025-06-19 03:01:43 UTC, which is the morning of June 19 in UTC but could read as June 18 evening in US Pacific time, likely explaining the date drift in secondary sources. A second, later Lütke tweet (status 1938270308563099971, June 26, 2025) exists and is sometimes conflated with the original June 19 post in casual citations; it is a follow-up, not the coining tweet.
relationship: Supports the 'prompt engineering is dead, context engineering is what matters now' framing, but the primary artifacts themselves are more measured than the framing that grew up around them: Lütke only says he 'likes the term... better,' and Karpathy frames it as context engineering being the real skill 'in every industrial-strength LLM app' while still describing prompts as a real (if narrower) category people use 'day-to-day.' Neither tweet declares prompt engineering dead or obsolete; that stronger claim is a later embellishment added by secondary commentary, not present in the origin artifacts.
derivative_of: Not a repackaging of a prior paper or benchmark; it is a terminological proposal. Karpathy's tweet is explicitly derivative of Lütke's in that it is a direct public endorsement/extension of Lütke's specific wording six days earlier, adding Karpathy's own technical elaboration of what filling the context window involves.
register: practitioner/engineer (both authors are addressing an audience of people building LLM applications day to day, via a casual, informal social-media register rather than an academic or enterprise-buyer one)
notes: Dates and posting order were verified independently of secondary paraphrase by decoding the Twitter/X snowflake IDs embedded in each status URL, which gave June 19, 2025 for Lütke and June 25, 2025 for Karpathy, both consistent with the task description's claimed dates and the 'six days later' gap. The exact verbatim tweet text could not be re-confirmed by directly loading x.com in this pass (x.com returned an error to automated fetch), so the quoted text above relies on search-engine snippets that themselves purport to quote the tweets directly; treat verbatim wording as [uncertain] pending a manual check of the live posts.
new_angle: Pins the coining event to two specific, dated, independently-timestamp-verified tweets rather than the vague 'mid-2025' most outlets use, and flags that the primary artifacts are more hedged ('I really like the term... better,' 'the delicate art and science of filling the context window') than the 'prompt engineering is dead' framing commonly attributed to them, which is useful ammunition for a counterpoint piece like 'Context engineering didn't retire the prompt.' Also flags a secondary Lütke tweet (June 26) that gets conflated with the original in casual citation.
